_: EXP-1196/1218/1219: THE device readiness block, one spec x5 (web, desktop, iOS, Android, CLI). A device builds `doctor` (coding::device_doctor) and sends it on register + heartbeat; the server stores it in devices.doctor (synced). Every client renders the SAME block from it: groups as filled bands, one flat row per item (state glyph, label, detail, at most one action). No subtitles, no footers with sentences. The device writes `detail`; clients never compose it.

copy.importBody: Your login moves into Exponential. Sign in again outside of it.

rules: The computer_use item IS the switch row: label + switch, no glyph, no detail. Its switch writes launch_defaults.computerUse. state off = switch off; ok/action = on.
Items with `parent` (the OS permission rows) render indented under their parent and only while the parent is not off.

An action renders as ONE trailing pill. On the device itself every action is offered. For ANOTHER device only actions with remote=true are offered (update -> device command agent_update {agent}; sign_in -> the existing remote agent_login flow); a non-remote action renders no pill.
The primary (filled) pill is the action of the first `action`/`error` row whose action is OFFERED in that context (on another device a non-remote action is skipped); all others are plain pills.
Nothing is runnable while a `required` item is not ok; otherwise the runnable agents are the `agents` items in state ok.
A group's `tag` renders verbatim (lowercase `optional`) as the band's trailing muted text.
Rows that need attention = state `action` or `error`; `missing` and `off` never count as a problem.
A missing optional agent is `missing` (grey dash), never red. `error` (red) is only for a missing REQUIRED item.
The composer shows, for the picked device + agent when that agent cannot run there, ONLY that agent's row (same row, same action) under the composer; when Git is the failure, the Git row.
The first-run footer shows `continue` (filled) instead of `skip` when Git is ok and at least one agent is runnable; `recheck` always.

A device row with doctor = null (a stale offline row: the device has not registered since it got the doctor) renders no block; device settings then still shows the bare Computer use switch row (no description) so the switch stays reachable.

EXP-1232: Codex is a MANAGED download — the device fetches the pinned build on the first sign-in, so its row never reads Not installed and never offers install. No login and no binary = missing · Signed out · sign_in (grey, never a problem; the sign-in fetches). A stored login with the fetch running = action · Downloading… with no pill. A failed fetch = action · Download failed · update (re-fetches; agent_update codex on another device).

No ambient logins: runs only ever use the device's account profiles (one per email). An agent row whose CLI has an AMBIENT login (~/.claude, ~/.codex) carries `import` = that login's email: it renders an `import` pill BEFORE its action pill (same offer rules; on another device -> agent_login {agent, import: true}, cap agent-import). The pill confirms first: title importTitle, body importBody, buttons Cancel / Import. Import MOVES the login (the ambient one is signed out).

Every sign-in lands on the profile whose email it signed in as: an email already on the device refreshes THAT profile (and only it) and shows the alreadyAdded warning toast; a new email adds a profile.

EXP-1273: computer use is foreground only on X11, macOS and Windows. A session the device cannot drive (a Wayland session, no display) renders the computer_use row as `missing` with the DEVICE's reason as its detail (e.g. 'Wayland session: computer use needs an X11 session for now.'); `unavailable` is the detail only when the device gives no reason.

NEW-78: the voice group's ONE row is `microphone`, and only the IDE adds it: on the member's voice device (user_voice_settings.voice_device_id) with Push to talk on; everywhere else (and the CLI daemon always) there is no voice band. States: ok · Granted; action · Not granted · grant; missing · No input device (grey, no pill). On macOS `grant` asks for access while the OS has not asked yet, else opens System Settings → Privacy → Microphone; Linux and Windows have no microphone permission, so an input device there = ok · Granted. `grant` is local-only, and the row never touches `runnable`.
